title: What to see in Los Cabos: 5 places from the Arch to San José
description: Five Los Cabos places: the Arch, El Médano, Chileno, Santa María and San José, with practical advice on beach choices, access and transfers.
keyword: what to see in Los Cabos
relatedQueries: things to do in Los Cabos
what to see in Los Cabos itinerary
intro: When choosing what to see in Los Cabos, distinguish Cabo San Lucas, the Tourist Corridor’s beaches and San José del Cabo. This guide develops five places with different characters: the Arch, El Médano, Chileno, Santa María and San José’s historic centre.

The selection combines coastal scenery and town life without claiming every beach is safe every day or that all excursions have identical inclusions. Each place has its own documentary archive photograph. Use the visiting blocks to compare choices and reserve only the experience that suits your trip.

sections.heading: 1. The Arch: choose the outing before boarding
paragraphs: The Arch is Cabo San Lucas’s recognisable rock formation in the Land’s End area. The tourism office presents it as an emblem of the peninsula’s meeting marine landscapes. The documentary photograph was taken from the water: a close view like this requires choosing a boat service rather than simply finding a pedestrian approach across the rocks.

Compare the boarding point, duration, equipment, stops and cancellation conditions before booking. A photograph of the Arch does not establish that an excursion includes landings, meals or activities. Wind and waves can change operations. Do not try to replace a cancelled outing with an unauthorised approach. If your interest is simply seeing the coastal setting, distinguish that objective from purchasing a longer package with services you may not need.

sections.heading: 2. El Médano: an urban beach in Cabo San Lucas
paragraphs: El Médano sits within Cabo San Lucas, combining beach, services and views towards surrounding rock formations. The tourism office locates it in the heart of town. It can suit a waterfront walk with urban activity nearby rather than a transfer to a corridor cove merely for a short break.

Restaurants and activities do not make every service free or guarantee a quiet stretch. Before booking a boat or activity from the beach, check the operator, equipment and permitted area. Follow flags and local instructions for swimming. A promotional description is not a permanent safety guarantee. The archive image shows the sand and coast without establishing today’s waves, boats or visitor numbers. Choose the experience you actually want instead of assuming every advertised activity belongs in the same outing.

sections.heading: 3. Chileno Beach: an outing along the Tourist Corridor
paragraphs: Chileno Beach lies along the Tourist Corridor between Los Cabos’ main centres. The official source associates it with swimming and snorkelling and describes amenities including palapas, parking and toilets. The practical choice is identifying the actual entrance and deciding how much time to spend here, rather than assuming it is beside every hotel in the region.

Confirm which services operate for your date and how you will return if relying on transport. Relative proximity to Santa María can help you choose between them. It does not require visiting both or turn the road into a comfortable pedestrian connection. Check swimming conditions locally. An older coastal image does not establish underwater visibility, calm water or available rentals. If snorkelling interests you, confirm equipment and rules before purchasing an activity.

sections.heading: 4. Santa María Beach: a different cove landscape
paragraphs: Santa María offers a cove framed by granite formations along the same corridor. The tourism office describes its marine setting and access by road or boat outings. Its appeal is the bay landscape and a coastal experience different from El Médano’s urban frontage, rather than identical sea conditions every day.

Use the authorised entrance and follow local instructions even when a brochure describes calm waters. For a boat excursion, check inclusions and whether the stop depends on conditions. Arriving by road requires planning parking or pickup. A nearby hotel does not automatically provide access to all its facilities. The photograph identifies the cove without certifying present-day water conditions or suitability for every person in your group. It is reasonable to enjoy the setting without entering the sea.

sections.heading: 5. San José del Cabo’s historic centre: streets and art beyond the beach
paragraphs: San José del Cabo is a separate centre from Cabo San Lucas, with a historic church and surroundings associated with galleries and art. The tourism office distinguishes their profiles within Los Cabos. Give the stop time for streets, buildings and public spaces rather than treating it as a quick visit to the same place where you boarded for the Arch.

The photograph shows the central church, not a performance or current event. For an organised gallery walk or an evening activity, confirm the calendar and participating businesses for your date. An Art Walk evening is not presented as a daily event or guaranteed admission to every gallery. Arrange return transport too. An afternoon in the historic centre requires different planning from remaining at the beach beside your accommodation.

sections.heading: Two centres, one corridor and different budgets
paragraphs: Los Cabos is a region in Baja California Sur, rather than an island or the name of one beach. Cabo San Lucas and San José del Cabo play different roles in this route. When choosing accommodation or an airport, check the exact address and complete journey to your activities. A booking containing the word Cabo does not settle its location.

There is no single fare for these five places. Urban walks, beaches, purchases and an Arch outing involve different spending. Separate transfers, parking, activities and meals and check each inclusion. Sources were consulted on 5 November 2026. Recheck maritime and access notices before departure rather than treating an archive photograph as a report of sea conditions.

itinerary: Cabo San Lucas block: choose an outing towards the Arch or a walk at El Médano, or combine them with a realistic buffer for boarding, return and a meal. Establish where the boat service starts and finishes first.
Corridor block: choose Chileno or Santa María according to access, conditions and services. Seeing both requires arranging a transfer rather than assuming a continuous sandy path connects them.

Urban block: give San José del Cabo a separate outing. Explore the centre and check any gallery activity before building the afternoon around it. A short stay can choose two blocks without completing every item.

faq.question: Are Los Cabos and Cabo San Lucas the same?
faq.answer: Los Cabos is the regional destination. Cabo San Lucas is one main centre, while San José del Cabo is another with a different historic centre and character.

faq.question: Can you walk right up to the Arch?
faq.answer: A close view of the formation from the water requires arranging a boat outing. We do not recommend seeking an unauthorised route across rocks.

faq.question: Do these beaches guarantee safe swimming?
faq.answer: No. Check conditions, flags and local instructions on the day. Tourism descriptions and photographs do not replace that check.

faq.question: Does Art Walk take place every day?
faq.answer: It is not presented here as a daily activity. Confirm the calendar and gallery participation for your intended San José outing.

conclusion: Choose beaches for their actual access and conditions and leave time for San José. A useful combination avoids unnecessary transfers and distinguishes a simple walk from a purchased service.
